posts.description:
Last Saturday, I went to an NVIDIA warm-up event for GTC Berlin and drank beer brewed by AI agents. 🦞🍺

Gerhard runs Lobster Lager. Agents built his website and handle the logistics, the ingredients, the recipes and the brewing. What they still haven't automated: taxes. Very German.

His line stuck with me: "If I, at 68, can use this, imagine what you could be doing."

As a DevRel, I was just as hooked on how Mark Heaps ran the room. He turned every transition into a story, brought a bit of Texas to Berlin, and never pitched once. He put builders on stage and let them do the inspiring. Honestly, a masterclass in developer storytelling.

Want to build something yourself? Here are some free resources from the event:
- Build-a-Claw Resource Hub: https://lnkd.in/dyk89aAK
- Free NemoClaw & OpenShell course: https://lnkd.in/dChQ6_tG
- NVIDIA NemoClaw GitHub: https://lnkd.in/dfDSdNKR

Cheers!

posts.description:
Every morning I take the Springfield line to uni and change to a bus. If the train is 3 minutes late, do I run, or have I already missed it? 🏃‍♀️
No app answered that, so I built one.
Stopwise shows every train, bus, tram and ferry in South East Queensland live, using TransLink's real-time data. Choose your train and where you get off, and it rates every bus after it: Make it, Tight or Miss, based on the real walking route and live delays.
Under the hood:
🔹 An Express server fetches TransLink's feeds once every 30 seconds and shares them with every user, instead of every phone calling TransLink
🔹 PostgreSQL holds the timetable for 12,000+ stops
🔹 A scheduled job records how late every train is every 10 minutes, so you can see which lines and times you can actually rely on
🔹 "Start journey" walks you through the trip and alerts you when to get off, even with your phone locked
The bug I won't forget: after adding security headers, the map looked fine – until I zoomed in and OpenStreetMap started blocking every new tile. The headers had stopped sending information their servers require, and cached tiles hid the problem on the first screen. Now I test the whole user journey after every change, not just the first page.
It began as "Railway Live" with only trains. Once buses, trams and ferries came in, it needed a new name.
Try it or read the code 👇
